how_to_read: entities = new entities in full map form, each to be copied into a part by merge_fixes.mjs if accepted (S4's form). edits = changes to merged entities (retire, move a point, change a support, rewrite a what), each with its evidence. reviewed = the merge's listed items settled with no change to points or supports (an optional note_add for the entity). seen_not_proposed = painted marks looked at and left out, with why. entities.name: narrow empty skiff under the arch's south foot
entities.what: A long, narrow, empty skiff lying in the water under the south half of the arch, parallel to the south bank: a slim hull seen side-on, about 340 px long, its sharp west end running in behind the arch's south leg and its east end rising to an upturned stem with a small knob on its tip; four short uprights (frames or thwarts) stand between gunwale and bottom over its east half. No crew, oar, pole or mooring line is painted.
entities.vis: part: its west end runs in behind the arch's south leg (u ~18915-18935); the south-east end post crosses it at u ~19015
entities.note: SECOND PASS (middle): replaces S3.prop.floating_timber_19090 (edit below: retire it). Strokes on contrast crops at zoom 3-4: gunwale (top line) (18933, 947) -> (19014, 964) -> (19100, 975) -> (19160, 975) -> (19252, 945); bottom (18933, 961) -> (19014, 983) -> (19100, 1000) -> (19160, 997) -> (19255, 967). The depth grows from ~14 px in the west to ~25 px at u 19100-19160, then both lines rise together into a stem whose tip carries a small knob at (19250-19260, 943-952), with a short post down to (19258, 965). Uprights between the lines at u 19108-19113, 19160-19170, 19185-19192 and 19210-19215 (v ~970-1000). This is a hull's profile: a log or spar keeps one depth along its length and has no rising stem. BOW: the upturned stem is east, so front = the waterline under it; the west end is sharp and hidden, rear est where the two lines meet behind the arch's leg. pose 'moored' is a reading: nothing ties it and nobody is in it; it lies ~40-60 px north of the south bank's est shore (v ~1040), under the ridge of S3.bld.mat_shed_19160. OTHER READINGS, kept: a long timber or spar afloat (river_e's first reading), or a footing timber of the bridge's south abutment (river_e); neither explains the stem with its knob. t7 and the bridge agent also read a skiff. OWNER: its main point (front, u 19255) falls in the east range; the merge listed it for the middle pass. SCALE CUE: hull ~340 px long (4.4 m at 77 px/m), ~20-25 px deep. Crops: scratchpad/S3_second_middle/i_timber.jpg, i_timber_e.jpg, i_timber_w.jpg, i_timber_m.jpg.

reviewed.item: the 35 `bridge deck` entities west of u 18810: ramp or bank
reviewed.decision: keep all 35 on `bridge deck` (the ramp). No support change.
reviewed.evidence: No west edge is inked, but the line where the south ramp's crowd meets the water is the deck's far edge, not a bank: measured at the same v, it runs 696-776 px west of the painted deck_e from v 400 to v 965 (the crowd's edge west of the seated man (18560, 400): 725; the bridge agent's (18300, 700): 696; river_w's bank points (18300, 640): 737, (18230, 775): 718, (18180, 890): 709, (18080, 965): 776), following the arch's convex flank (deck_e's slope changes from -2.0 to -1.4 over that range). A natural bank would not keep a constant offset from the bridge's near face along a curve. All 35 lie inside that edge (their offsets from deck_e at their own v are 98-676 px) and above the bridge agent's foot line (v ~1090). The boat moored at the edge fits: its stern hood ends at (18200, 770), 750 px west of deck_e, i.e. on the edge line, so the boat lies alongside the ramp's west foot. The westernmost cluster (the white-jacket man, the seated man in a cap, the bending man, the crouching figure, offsets 582-676) stands on the ramp's edge over the boat; the tray stall they gather round is one scene with them and stays on the deck too. Their H then comes from the v rule (u* = max(u, u_s(v)), or the lead's H_profile_X), 1.6-2.9 m by the bridge agent's primary foot; if the deck lands higher on its near face (the bridge agent's third column, foot at (18905, 862)), the same entities get 0-1 m. That choice is the bridge's foot, not these entities' support. The 'west railing piece' is no evidence either way (edit on S3.str.rainbow_bridge).

lessons: **Test a hidden deck edge by its offset from the painted edge at the same v.** On S3 the line where the south ramp's crowd meets the water stays 696-776 px west of the near railing's edge from v 400 to v 965 while that edge curves (slope -2.0 to -1.4): a natural bank would not follow the arch, so it is the deck's far edge, and a slatted panel 590-670 px out is inside the deck, not its railing.

**Read a parasol's hub where its ribs meet, at zoom 3 on a stretched crop.** Two S3 parasols had the hub at a canopy end (where a man's hands are, or a guess), 36 and 86 px from the ribs' meeting point, and their est bases followed it.

**Profile a long thin floating shape before naming it.** A timber keeps one depth along its length; a hull deepens toward its middle, rises to a stem and shows frames (S3's 'floating timber' under the arch is a skiff).

**A dark mass joined to a figure in the same tone, with no head, ears or legs of its own, is that figure's clothing.** S3's third 'donkey' at the bridge's foot was the calling man's two wide sleeves; look for the animal's legs and body where they would have to be.
**A boat's fittings bound its ends.** A recorded stern that falls under the boat's own stern hood is too short: put the rear under the hood's far end.
